lines: 6-month history of distressing thoughts about contamination with germs and excessive hand washing

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a history of mild persistent asthma and seasonal allergic rhinitis, previously evaluated in Internal Medicine and Otolaryngology earlier this year, who presents to the Psychiatry clinic with a 6-month history of distressing thoughts about contamination with germs.
She reports spending several hours a day washing her hands and cleaning her home to alleviate her fear of infection.
She recognizes these fears as excessive and irrational but feels compelled to perform these actions to reduce her anxiety.

encounters.cc: Ongoing trouble managing daily stress with persistent anxiety and feeling constantly on edge for 10-12 months

lines: Ongoing trouble managing daily stress with persistent anxiety and feeling constantly on edge for 10-12 months

The patient is a 31-year-old female with a known history of obsessive-compulsive disorder, mild persistent asthma, and seasonal allergic rhinitis who returns to the psychiatry clinic for ongoing management of anxiety symptoms.

She was last evaluated in this department approximately six months prior for distressing thoughts regarding contamination with associated excessive hand washing, and now explains that for the past 10–12 months, she has felt "constantly on edge," even when nothing in particular is wrong.
She says her thoughts often race about worst-case scenarios, including minor things like whether she forgot to unplug her curling iron or whether her car tires might burst during a short drive.
She reports difficulty falling asleep most nights and sometimes wakes up in the middle of the night, her mind filled with unfinished to-do lists or imagined emergencies.
She describes fatigue during the day, difficulty concentrating at work, and increasingly frequent tension headaches.

Although her job as a graphic designer allows flexibility, she finds herself mentally exhausted by midday and has begun avoiding team meetings due to a fear of being judged if she forgets to contribute something important.
She recently spent three weeks traveling out of state, hoping a change of scenery would provide some relief.
She visited friends in Colorado, drove through Utah to visit national parks, and finished the trip in Arizona for a desert pottery retreat.
Though she enjoyed these activities at times, she admits the anxiety persisted during the trip—she even spent hours comparing emergency vet clinics online when one of her friend's dogs had diarrhea.
- Albuterol sulfate HFA 90 mcg inhaled, 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Fluticasone propionate HFA 44 mcg inhaled, 2 puffs twice daily
- Sumatriptan 50 mg orally as needed for migraine headache (maximum 200 mg per day)
Seasonal environmental allergens (tree and grass pollens), No known drug allergies
She's developed a growing interest in collecting rare hot sauces from each region she visits and has over 200 bottles displayed in her kitchen.
Twice a week, she attends a local pottery studio, which she finds therapeutic when she can focus.
She also recently began investing in contemporary art through an online platform, though she says the decision has created more stress than she anticipated.
She drinks socially but does not use recreational drugs.
She is in a stable relationship.
On review of systems, she denies panic attacks, compulsions, hallucinations, or flashbacks.
Her appetite is normal, though she's noticed some jaw tension and mild nausea during especially anxious days.
On mental status exam, she appears mildly restless but cooperative, with appropriate affect and logical thought processes.
She agrees to begin treatment and expresses a desire to avoid medication that causes sedation or dependence.

lines: Follow-up for persistent anxiety with new complaint of decreased libido and sexual dysfunction since starting sertraline
